Why none of the obvious fixes work

Email them. Delete them. Or do nothing. None of it works.

There are basically three things you can do about the dormant half of your list. Each one has a failure mode, and the dashboard you’d use to check whether it’s working is the same dashboard that didn’t tell you the truth in the first place.

Mail them anyway

Whether you set up a sunset flow in Klaviyo or batch a re-engagement campaign yourself, you’re sending to a segment with a high bounce risk and an unknown number of spam-trap addresses sprinkled through it. Send too fast and bounces spike before you can hit pause. Send slow enough to be safe and you’re hand-pacing tens of thousands of emails one at a time, monitoring four mailbox providers, ready to abort the second any threshold trips. No human does this for long.

And the part that should worry you most: even if it works, you can’t tell. Real opens and phantom opens look identical. You’ll see a number go up and assume you won.

Delete them

List cleaners and sunset flows do this. They remove the cold segment, your engagement rate climbs on paper, and your ESP bill drops. Two problems.

First, some of those subscribers would have come back with the right approach at the right pace; you’re writing off acquisition cost you already paid.

Second, deletion doesn’t fix the underlying mechanism. Your deliverability is shaped by how you mail your list, not just who is on it. A clean list mailed badly degrades the same way a dirty list does.

Do nothing

This is what most lists are running. The bleed compounds: every month, more subscribers cross into dormant, your engagement rate slips a little further, more of your real buyers slide into spam.

And because you can’t see it happening, you don’t know when the slope steepens. By the time the revenue drop is undeniable, the recovery is much harder than it would have been a year ago.

The answer

So what does safe re-engagement actually look like?

You don’t change your ESP. You don’t touch your sending domain. ReEngage Pro connects to your existing platform, reads your engagement data, and handles the three things no human can do consistently: confirm there’s a real mailbox behind each address before it sends, pace the sends slow enough to protect your reputation, and adjust automatically when something looks wrong. The default settings are conservative. Start a campaign without changing a single setting and your domain is protected from day one.

Default pacing is conservative. When you have a broadcast scheduled, you can bump up the speed in real time and dial it back afterward. A broadcast’s volume gives the system more room to work safely.

The protection mechanism

If you can’t detect the damage, dilute it.

Apple Mail Privacy shows opens that didn’t happen. Gmail hides complaints that did. When a subscriber marks a re-engagement email as spam in Gmail, the complaint never gets reported back to your ESP. You can’t see those complaints. Nothing can.

But Gmail doesn’t flag your domain on the count of complaints. It flags you on the percentage. So instead of trying to detect what nothing can see, ReEngage Pro changes the denominator.

Without dilution
150 re-engagement emails
4 complaints
9× Gmail’s 0.3% flag threshold. Reputation damage in motion before anyone notices.
With dilution
150 inside a 30,000 broadcast
Same 4 complaints
Well under the line that triggers damage. Invisible to the metric that flags you.

Same complaints. Same subscribers. Completely different reputation outcome. The denominator does the work.

Booster Mode

When ReEngage Pro sees your broadcast going out to your engaged list, it accelerates the re-engagement queue to ride underneath that volume. Cold-list sends move at one-to-two-second intervals during the cover window. Your re-engagement campaign goes faster precisely when it’s safest to do so.

Wait State

When no broadcast cover is available, the engine refuses to ship a small isolated batch that would spike your Postmaster percentage. It waits for the next broadcast window instead of degrading your reputation in the silent interval. You can override if a campaign needs to ship on its own schedule.

An honest note about how this works. Dilution coverage scales with how often you broadcast. If you mail your engaged list weekly, the system has plenty of cover windows to work inside. If you broadcast rarely, coverage is limited and the engine falls back to throttle-only safety. If you’re not sure how often you actually broadcast, the first week of your trial will tell you.
